story.what_it_does: Waaree Energies makes solar modules and is expanding into cells, ingots and wafers, batteries, inverters, transformers, solar glass and green hydrogen electrolysers. FY26 consolidated revenue was ₹26,536.77 crore, up 83.72%. It sells in India and abroad, including the US, and retail sales are a growing share.
story.plans: Management guides FY27 operating EBITDA of ₹7,000-7,700 crore and plans about ₹30,000 crore of capex across its business lines. Near-term plans include a 10 GW cell facility going live in Q3 and Q4 FY27, US module capacity of 4.8 GW by March 2027, and a 20 GWh battery plant by FY28.
story.moat: The notes show scale: 25.8 GW of installed module capacity, a large order book of about ₹59,200 crore, and a push into cells and other products. The notes also list dependence on Chinese imports as a threat, and they describe no clear pricing power, since management expects module price correction in India next year.

scenarios.story: New cell capacity ramps up, utilisation recovers to 80-85% and the order book converts, with H2 delivering 55-60% of the FY27 guidance. Net cash and strong operating cash flow help fund the heavy capex.
signals_to_watch: Module capacity utilisation rising toward 80-85% over the next 2-3 quarters
10 GW cell capacity going live in two tranches in Q3 and Q4 FY27

scenarios.story: Revenue keeps growing but margins stay near the 18% level seen in recent quarters, and results lean on a stronger second half. FY27 EBITDA guidance of ₹7,000-7,700 crore is held but needs a big H2.
signals_to_watch: H2 operating EBITDA reaching 55-60% of FY27 guidance

scenarios.story: Policy shifts and the US Section 232 uncertainty cause more export order cancellations, while the US customs investigation and an expected price correction in India squeeze margins. Heavy capex and weaker utilisation could then pressure returns.
signals_to_watch: Further US export orders dropped from the reported order book
Module capacity utilisation staying below 50%, as in Q2 FY27
